remarks_1999: Metropolitan Museum of Art files include original label, "White Barn (Canadian) No. 2/1932/(oil) by Georgia O'Keeffe" (Alfred Stieglitz, An American Place1, black ink). Whitney Archive indicates, "'Infor. From Miss Bry (An Amer. Place), July 1949: On permanent loan to the Metropolitan Museum of Art from Georgia O'Keeffe as part of the Alfred Stieglitz Coll." Whitney Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks indicate that painting was in 1933 New York (An American Place) exhibition, as no. 7, *White Barn 2*, but no. 7 in that show is cat. no. 805. This work, cat. no. 808 or cat. no. 809 was possibly no. 14. Pictured in 1935 New York (An American Place) Stieglitz installation photograph, see Appendix III, figure 61. See also cat. nos. 805, 806, 808, 809. Reproduced and titled *Barn No. 2* in *Creative Art* (April 1933); *White Barn* in *Life* (February 1938) and *Modern American Paintings* (1939); *White Barn (Canadian) No. 2 (Gaspé Peninsula – Canada* in *Knight Publications*, plate 10, 1937); reproduced in *Bulletin of the Art Institute of Chicago* (February 1943); untitled in *USA* (1945); reproduced and titled *White Canadian Barn* in The *Philadelphia Museum Bulletin* (May 1945); *The White Barn* in *MKR's Art Outlook* (1946). (Source: Lynes, 1999)

titles.title: White Canadian Barn, No. 2

description: A bright white, low barn with a bluish-black pitched roof stretches across the frame. The barn has two large, black doors, one on the left and one on the right side of the building. Only one side of the structure is visible, and it stands on a stripe of green earth. A blue sky hangs overhead.
